record.original_question: For an integer m > 5, determine the smallest integer n such that every set of n points in space with no four coplanar contains m points lying on a common sphere. Ask the analogous question for other prescribed spatial figures such as cones or cubes, and for the planar version with m > 4 and no three points collinear.

evidence.quote: Let m > 5 an integer. Find a minimum n ... such that ... there exist m ones among these which belong to a surface of a sphere. (b) Same question for an arbitrary spatial figure ... (c) Similar problems in plane.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let m > 5 be a fixed integer. A set of points in three-dimensional Euclidean space is said to be in general position if no four of them are coplanar. Determine the smallest positive integer n = n(m) with the following property: every set of n points in three-dimensional Euclidean space in general position (no four coplanar) contains m points that all lie on the surface of some common sphere.

Pose and study the analogous extremal problem when "sphere" is replaced by another prescribed spatial figure, e.g.:
(a) the lateral surface of a (circular) cone,
(b) the surface (boundary) of a cube,
or other fixed surfaces F in three-dimensional space — that is, find the smallest n such that every n points in general position contain m points lying on a common copy of F.

Pose and study the planar analogue: for m > 4, determine the smallest integer n such that every set of n points in the plane, no three of which are collinear, contains m points lying on a common circle (and, more generally, on a common copy of a prescribed planar figure such as a conic, square, etc.).
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches for this specific Erdős–Szekeres-type problem—forcing m cospherical points among n points in general position in three-space, and its analogues for cones, cubes, and the planar (cocircular) version—did not return any source establishing a determination of the extremal function or a definitive solution. The status appears to be unresolved in the literature accessible via the search, but no authoritative confirmation either way was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Erdős–Szekeres-type extremal problems; no mention of an exact value for forcing m cospherical points among points in general position in space.
status_evidence.claim: No determination of the cospherical extremal function is reported in standard Erdős–Szekeres surveys.

status_evidence.snippet: Catalog of Erdős problems on distances and configurations; the specific cospherical-points-in-general-position problem is not listed as resolved.
